raw_title: “Living Amoeba of an Organization”: Organizational Bricolage as an Adaptive Strategy in Digital Journalism
raw_abstract: Journalism’s future is often narrated through disruption and decline, yet this framing obscures the everyday creativity through which newswork persists under constraint. This article advances organizational bricolage as a lens for understanding adaptation in journalism, shifting attention from crisis-driven reactions to the generative practices through which journalists and newsrooms continually reconfigure themselves. Drawing on a multi-site ethnographic case study of three Monothematic News Organizations, the study shows how bricolage operates both at inception and in daily practice. Through anchoring in recognizable journalistic values, augmenting with nonprofit and alternative repertoires, and differentiating from antagonistic elements, MNOs craft legitimacy, resilience, and distinct editorial identities. Far from being resistant to change, journalists emerge as bricoleurs, improvising with the resources at hand to sustain mission-driven reporting. Theoretically, the study positions bricolage as a critical framework for rethinking adaptation, not as a reactive adjustment, but as an ongoing institutional formation. Practically, it highlights how bricolage enables small, precarious outlets to produce durable and innovative journalism, while also revealing its limitations amid the influence of funders, platform dominance, and systemic inequality. In doing so, the article reframes journalism as a profession that endures not despite uncertainty, but through continual acts of recomposition.
